rv_sites.label: Full-hookup RV sites
rv_sites.assumption: Sized to about 10 acres under the county's design rules: a 12 by 40 ft hardened pad per space, 20 ft between units, 20 ft two-way roads and 25 ft right-of-way setbacks [^3].

monthly_sites.label: Sites held for monthly stays
monthly_sites.assumption: About 40% of the RV sites. Monthly workforce demand is the deepest in Bastrop, but USDA B&I funds resort trailer parks and campgrounds, not residential trailer parks [^50], so the plan keeps most revenue from nightly and weekly stays.

cabins.label: Rental cabins
cabins.assumption: A small cabin line priced against the 12 state park cabins at $110 to $200 a night [^36] and Basin's $130 poolside apartment [^20].

land_acres.label: Site area, acres
land_acres.assumption: A hypothetical site of about 10 acres in the SH 71 and SH 21 trade area; no particular tract is assumed. Its jurisdiction and road access are conditions to confirm; the model assumes a site outside city limits.

land_per_acre.label: Land price per acre
land_per_acre.assumption: The research holds no closed land sale and no assessed land value for the trade area. $50,000 per acre is a placeholder that the lender must replace with an appraisal.

site_cost.label: Development cost per RV site
site_cost.assumption: ARVC's 2023 survey of new parks found 60% of respondents at $15,000 or more per full-hookup site and 20% at $30,000 or more [^58]. A Texas state filing for a 176-site resort in Wichita Falls estimated $3.5 million [^59]. Construction inputs rose 8.9% in the year to August 2026 [^60], and the county requires hardened pads, underground electric and fire-water storage [^3].

cabin_cost.label: Cost per cabin, set on site
cabin_cost.assumption: No per-cabin cost is published. Glamping operators reported an average start-up cost of $1,511,600 in 2025 [^65]; a delivered park-model cabin with deck and hookups is carried at $85,000.

amenity_building.label: Office, store, bathhouse and laundry
amenity_building.assumption: The county requires a service building for every 50 spaces plus one fixture set for each additional 30 [^3]. One building with office, camp store, restrooms, showers and laundry; no published cost benchmark.

contingency_pct.label: Hard-cost contingency
contingency_pct.assumption: 10% of hard cost for a ground-up park with septic, water and electric extensions not yet designed.

soft_pct.label: Soft costs, share of hard cost
soft_pct.assumption: Engineering, county IDP review, OSSF design, Houston toad plan fees [^5], legal and construction interest.

ffe.label: Cabin furnishings, store fixtures, golf carts and software

working_capital.label: Pre-opening and working capital
working_capital.assumption: Covers marketing, payroll and utilities in the months before the park reaches its Year 1 occupancy.

monthly_rate.label: Monthly site rent, before metered electric
monthly_rate.assumption: Operator-posted Bastrop monthly rents run $550 to $800 plus metered electric [^19,25,29,31,32]. $700 sits in the upper half for new 50-amp pull-through sites; rent grows about 3% a year, the growth rate Newmark's 2026 survey uses [^61].

monthly_occ.label: Occupancy of monthly sites
monthly_occ.assumption: Basin lists 49 of its 66 spaces as seasonal [^21] and the workforce base is growing [^41]; turnover keeps a monthly section below full.

nightly_rate.label: Blended nightly rate, transient sites
nightly_rate.assumption: Operator-posted nightly rates run $40 to $70, and weekly rates of $200 to $300 lower the blend [^19,24,25,29]. ARVC's 2023 median for full-hookup sites was $55 midweek and $58 on weekends [^58].

transient_occ.label: Occupancy of transient sites
transient_occ.assumption: ARVC's 2023 survey put full-hookup occupancy at 68% in months of operation [^58]. Transient demand is weaker in 2025 to 2026 at the listed REITs [^62,63] and on Campspot's platform [^64], so the ramp stops at 62%.

cabin_adr.label: Cabin average daily rate
cabin_adr.assumption: Inside the state park's $110 to $200 cabin range [^36] and below the national self-reported glamping cabin ADR of $338 [^65], because these are campground cabins, not luxury units.

cabin_occ.label: Cabin occupancy
cabin_occ.assumption: Leisure demand from Bastrop State Park, which reports that it often reaches capacity [^35], weighted to weekends and the spring, summer and fall season.

other_pct.label: Store, laundry, propane and storage, share of rent
other_pct.assumption: Ancillary revenue at a small park with a camp store; no local benchmark.

payroll.label: Payroll and benefits (Year 1)
payroll.assumption: A manager and about three full-time equivalents in season. ARVC's 2023 medians were 3 full-time and 2 part-time staff in the main season, $52,200 for a general manager and $15.01 an hour for general staff [^58]; carried here with growth to 2026 and payroll taxes, rising 3% a year.

utilities_pct.label: Utilities paid by the park, share of revenue
utilities_pct.assumption: Water, septic service, common electric and nightly-site electric; monthly sites pay metered electric as the local parks require [^19,29].

rm_pct.label: Repairs, maintenance and supplies, share of revenue
rm_pct.assumption: Roads, pads, pedestals, cabins and grounds.

marketing_pct.label: Marketing and booking fees, share of revenue
marketing_pct.assumption: Online booking platforms and listing fees on nightly and cabin revenue.

ga_pct.label: Administration, software and professional fees, share of revenue
ga_pct.assumption: Reservation software, accounting, legal and HOT filing.

mgmt_pct.label: Management fee, share of revenue
mgmt_pct.assumption: The research found no management fee norm for independent parks. 4% is carried so the projection pays for management even if the owner runs the park.

insurance.label: Insurance (Year 1)
insurance.assumption: Insurance terms were NOT FOUND. The 2011 fire burned 34,068 acres of the Lost Pines [^42]; the lender must replace this with a bound quote that includes wildfire.

tax_county.label: Bastrop County tax rate, FY 2026-27 ($0.4554 per $100)

bi_fee_pct.label: USDA guarantee fee, share of the guaranteed amount: 3.0% initial plus 0.50% for a guarantee issued before construction is complete

bi_annual_fee.label: USDA annual retention fee, share of guaranteed balance

bi_rate.label: Interest rate
bi_rate.assumption: B&I rates are negotiated between lender and borrower [^48]. Prime was 7.00% on October 9, 2026 [^66]; broker-reported 2026 RV park closings ran 6.74% to 7.16% [^67]. We carry Prime plus 0.75 points; the lender sets the rate at pricing

bi_amort_years.label: Amortization
bi_amort_years.assumption: USDA allows up to 40 years or the useful life of the project or collateral [^48]. Pads, roads and pedestals do not last 40 years, so we amortize over 25

bi_equity_min_pct.label: Minimum equity
bi_equity_min_pct.assumption: The research reads 7 CFR 5001.105 as requiring a new business to hold at least 20% to 25% tangible balance sheet equity or 25% of project cost [^51]. We test 25% of project cost; the lender must confirm the requirement in its credit memo.

bi_dscr_floor.label: Coverage floor
bi_dscr_floor.assumption: USDA sets no single coverage ratio for B&I; the lender's credit policy governs. We test 1.25x in Year 3, the first stabilized year.

growth_payroll.label: Payroll growth per year
growth_payroll.assumption: An allowance for park wages, which no Bastrop source tracks for campground staff; the ARVC medians [^58] are a 2023 snapshot, so the operator's staffing plan and local job postings should replace this before closing.

growth_insurance.label: Insurance growth per year
growth_insurance.assumption: An allowance for premium increases on a park among the Lost Pines, where the 2011 fire is the reference event [^42]; with no quote in hand, the carrier's bound terms set this line.

growth_tax.label: Taxable value growth per year
growth_tax.assumption: An allowance for reappraisal by the Bastrop Central Appraisal District, which values property at 100% of market [^14]; the study makes no forecast of the district's value, and county rate changes [^10,71] come on top.

usda_fee_paydown.label: Retention fee base decline per year
usda_fee_paydown.assumption: The annual retention fee is charged on the outstanding guaranteed balance; the model approximates amortization by lowering the base 3% of the original balance a year, a labelled simplification.

growth_reserve.label: Reserve growth per year
growth_reserve.assumption: The per-pad reserve grows 3% a year, a labelled allowance for replacement cost inflation.

uses.label: Soft costs, permits and construction interest

revenue.label: Monthly site rent
revenue.basis: sites x 12 x rent x occupancy

revenue.label: Nightly and weekly site rent
revenue.basis: sites x 365 x rate x occupancy

revenue.label: Cabin rent
revenue.basis: cabins x 365 x ADR x occupancy

opex.label: Property tax
opex.expr: (land_acres * land_per_acre + (rv_sites * site_cost + cabins * cabin_cost + amenity_building) * (1 + contingency_pct)) * (tax_county + tax_isd + tax_esd) * (1 + growth_tax) ** y

opex.label: USDA annual retention fee (passed through)
opex.expr: tpc * (1 - bi_equity_min_pct) * bi_guarantee_pct * bi_annual_fee * (1 - usda_fee_paydown * y)

proposed.note: the sponsor proposes a 25-year USDA-guaranteed loan for the balance
